name: MRL Equipment Company
old_description: MRL Equipment Co. Inc. has manufactured pavement marking, removal, grooving, and pavement maintenance equipment for over 36 years. Founded by road stripers with first-hand knowledge and background in striping and removal operations, MRL innovates with the customer to produce customized paint, thermoplastic, plural component, line removal/pavement grooving, water blasting, bituminous marking equipment and more.
about:
MRL Equipment Company operates from Billings, Montana, where it has built pavement marking, removal, grooving, and pavement maintenance equipment for more than three decades. The business was started by road stripers who brought first-hand experience from striping and removal operations, shaping a company that designs machinery around the practical needs of the people who use it daily.

The company produces a range of specialized trucks and systems, including thermoplastic applicators with 12,000‑lb and 16,000‑lb capacity, the EpoxyPro plural‑component impingement mixing system, removal and grooving trucks that use a multiple‑head progressive removal system to limit surface damage, and road marking and raised‑pavement‑marker equipment designed for high‑volume output and ease of service. MRL also offers retrofit kits, parts support, and financing options to keep fleets running.

Primary customers are pavement marking contractors, state and municipal highway departments, and striping crews who need reliable, high‑throughput equipment for line removal, groove cutting, water blasting, and bituminous marking applications. The company’s "built by stripers, for stripers" philosophy means each machine is developed with direct input from the operators who will run it.

MRL says its differentiation comes from designing equipment in collaboration with end users, resulting in features such as heated delivery systems that reduce downtime and a progressive removal head that balances speed with surface preservation. The focus on customization and operator‑centric design traces back to the founders’ own backgrounds in the trade.
